- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag in capturing momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 periods ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage price acceleration; increase forecast by 1–2% in final 5–7 days if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model underestimates; apply upward bias of 2–4% to compensate for suppressed volatility.
